Un sistema en equilibrio con un baño a t: A system in equilibrium with a bath at temperature $T$ occupies a state of energy $ε_i$ with probability proportional to $e^{−ε_i/k_B T}$. If the level has $g_i$ states, its weight is multiplied by $g_i$. Everything follows from the partition function:
La capacidad calorífica $C_V = dU/dT$ es: The heat capacity $C_V = dU/dT$ is the variance of the energy divided by $k_B T^2$. The energy is measured from the ground level; changing the origin does not change the populations.
Con dos niveles separados $ΔE$, la capac: With two levels separated by $ΔE$, the heat capacity has a maximum (the Schottky anomaly) when $k_B T$ is around $ΔE$. The quantum harmonic oscillator has levels $E_n = (n + 1/2)hν$ and $Z = 1/{1 − e^{−hν/k_B T}}$. Einstein used it for a solid: at high temperature $C_V → 3R$ (Dulong-Petit) and at low temperature the modes "freeze out" and $C_V → 0$. For a rigid rotor $E_J = B J(J+1)$ with $g = 2J+1$ and, at high temperature, $Z ≈ k_B T/B$.
Un <b>sólido de Einstein</b> con $N$ osc: An Einstein solid with $N$ oscillators and $q$ quanta has $Ω = binom(q + N − 1, q)$ microstates. The temperature comes from $1/T = ∂S/∂U$. If two solids share quanta, the distribution with the most microstates overwhelmingly dominates and that is where the temperatures become equal: it is the second law seen as pure counting. The Maxwell distribution of the speeds of a gas is in Ideal gases and cycles with entropy are in Thermodynamic cycles.
Qué no cubre esta herramienta: What this tool does not cover
Aquí se usa la estadística de <b>Maxwell: This tool uses Maxwell-Boltzmann statistics: each level has a population proportional to $g·e^{−ε/k_B T}$, valid for distinguishable particles (such as the oscillators of an Einstein solid) or for a dilute gas in which almost no state is occupied by more than one particle. There are no Fermi-Dirac statistics (fermions: only one electron per state, like the electrons in a metal) or Bose-Einstein statistics (bosons: photons, helium-4, condensates). This is a deliberate decision: those distributions need the chemical potential $μ$ and the density of states of the system, which depend on the total number of particles and on the geometry, and cannot be reduced to a list of levels with degeneracy. When the mean occupation number is much less than 1 (high temperature or low density) all three coincide with Maxwell-Boltzmann, which is the only case calculated here.
Parte de niveles de energía discretos y: It starts from discrete energy levels and the Boltzmann distribution (distinguishable particles or the levels of a system). It does not include Fermi-Dirac or Bose-Einstein statistics: it is not valid for degenerate quantum gases.
El sólido de Einstein da una sola frecue: The Einstein solid gives a single frequency for all the oscillators: it does not reproduce the Debye model at low temperature.
